newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - December 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - December 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Thursday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa selected to become Hong Kong's chief executive after colony's handover to Beijing in mid-1997.
Government to completely privatise state tobacco and alcohol monopoly bureau in three years.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - Police detain Chang Chung-teh, suspect in slaying of Taoyuan county magistrate and seven others.
Government to allow free trading of farmland in two years.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Communist China to announce two major conditions for its entry to World Trade Organisation.
Seven provincial banks to offer total of T$200 billion in low-interest loans to small businesses.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - Government to invest T$72 billion worth of postal funds in stock market.
Communist China says Taiwan should not even think about joining WTO before mainland.
LIBERTY TIMES - Ruling Nationalist Party vice-chairman Yu Kuo-hua accuses legislators of causing financial crisis through extravagant election campaigns.
Mainland Affairs Council says it will not rule out setting up "special channels of communication" with Hong Kong after chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa takes office.
